Salesforce (CRM) stock looks mispriced after the recent software sell-off, driven by fears that artificial intelligence (AI) will disrupt traditional enterprise software. The customer relationship management software provider enters this stretch from a position of financial strength, having generated $14.4 billion in free cash flow in Fiscal 2026. In the company's second-quarter Fiscal 2027 earnings release in August 2026, Chair and CEO Marc Benioff addressed the AI opportunity and pushed back against the disruption narrative, stating, "AI is delivering value across every layer of our platform."

I think investors are overlooking how little physical investment Salesforce needs to pursue that opportunity, with capex projected at roughly 1.5% of revenue in Fiscal 2027. Rather than being replaced, its software can become more useful and more embedded as enterprises adopt autonomous AI agents across workflows, in my view. Yet the market seems far more concerned about disruption. Ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings report on December 2, I rate CRM a Buy.

AI Exposure Without the Infrastructure Bill

What I like about Salesforce is that it offers AI exposure without the huge infrastructure bill. Now, Monday's rally following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia (NVDA) lifted CRM 2.7%. Yet shares remain roughly 26% below their August post-earnings level. Investors have sold software alongside companies facing enormous graphics processing unit (GPU) and power commitments, but Salesforce's spending requirements look very different.

For context, Salesforce's Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow reached $15 billion, with FCF of $14.4 billion. However, physical capex consumed only about 4% of operating cash. Its most recent Q2 FY27 results repeated the pattern, with $1.3 billion of operating cash and $1.1 billion of FCF.

We are seeing that Salesforce can keep developing Agentforce without committing tens of billions to new data centers. That leaves more flexibility for shareholder-friendly capital allocation, including ongoing share buybacks and its quarterly dividend. I find that appealing, especially as infrastructure financing has become such a concern elsewhere in the technology sector.

Trading disclosure
Salesforce earnings to put Bank of America's growth outlook to the test Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Salesforce Inc (NYSE:CRM, XETRA:FOO) remains rated "buy" at Bank of America, which sees a favorable short-term outlook for the stock after a roughly 27% decline from its September peak.

The comapny is set to report its fiscal 2027 third-quarter results on December 2, and the bank is looking for signs of faster organic growth in the second half, momentum in cRPO and bookings, and stronger Agentforce monetization.

Bank of America projects Salesforce's organic revenue growth will rise to 7.4% in the third quarter and 9.9% in the fourth, from 6.4% in the second.

The bank also forecasts third-quarter growth of 13.7% in current remaining performance obligations, or cRPO, on a constant-currency basis.

Learn more about Salesforce Inc

Read more about Salesforce Inc

Largely because of higher AI consumption costs, the bank expects third-quarter gross margin to fall 30 basis points and operating margin to fall 110 basis points year over year.

Bank of America's partner checks pointed to muted core seat growth in the calendar third quarter of 2026, while cross-selling and regional rollouts supported higher total contract values.

Those checks also indicated Salesforce customers were expanding Agentforce deployments where they saw value, while Data Cloud implementation activity remained strong.

Customers are gradually moving AI pilots into production as they assess token consumption costs and prepare their data before expanding paid use, according to partner feedback.

Autodesk, Inc. ADSK reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $3.20 per share, up 19.9% year over year. The figure surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.07 by 4.2%, aided by strong renewal rates, operating leverage and benefits from sales optimization.

Revenues increased 17% year over year to $2.16 billion, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.13 billion by 1.4%.

On a constant-currency basis, revenues grew 14%. Strength in construction and emerging markets supported results. Net revenue retention approximated the top end of the 100%-110% range in constant currency.

ADSK's Q3 Top-Line Details

Subscription revenues increased 17.3% year over year to $2.07 billion, while Other revenues rose 1.2% to $87 million. Autodesk reclassified certain consumption-based offerings as subscription revenues, with prior-period figures adjusted accordingly.

Region-wise, Americas revenues increased 18% year over year to $967 million, while EMEA revenues rose 17% to $838 million. APAC revenues advanced 12% to $355 million.

Autodesk, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Autodesk, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Autodesk, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Autodesk, Inc. Quote

Billings grew 12% year over year to $2.07 billion, or 13% in constant currency. ADSK signed its largest-ever enterprise business agreement (EBA) and completed several EBA renewals during the quarter.

The impact of the sales reorganization continued to diminish across most regions, although Western Europe remained slower to normalize. The new transaction model no longer provided a meaningful benefit to quarterly revenue and billings growth.

Autodesk's Product Portfolio in Detail

Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) revenues increased 19% year over year to $1.10 billion. Construction maintained strong momentum, supported by customers expanding their adoption of Autodesk's connected project workflows.

AutoCAD and AutoCAD LT revenues grew 11% year over year to $525 million. Manufacturing revenues increased 13% to $403 million, with Fusion benefiting from larger deployments and the integration of design and manufacturing workflows.

Other product revenues climbed 35% year over year to $135 million. The newly introduced product family includes Media and Entertainment and Autodesk Operations Solutions.

MaintainX generated nearly $33 million in revenues in its first quarter under Autodesk's ownership, exceeding management's expectations. ADSK plans to expand MaintainX across additional geographies and customer segments in the next fiscal year.

title: Adobe's Cash Flow Strengthens: Can It Support Bigger Share Buybacks?
detail:
Adobe's Cash Flow Strengthens: Can It Support Bigger Share Buybacks?
Anirudha Bhagat

ADBE
CRM
ADSK
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Adobe Inc.'s ADBE cash generation is giving it room to return money to shareholders. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, operating cash flow reached a record $2.52 billion, up from $2.20 billion a year earlier. After $85 million in capital spending, estimated free cash flow was about $2.44 billion. This performance provides a base for continued share repurchases.

Adobe returned $2.23 billion through buybacks during the quarter and repurchased approximately 9.5 million shares. In the first three quarters of fiscal 2026, the company generated operating cash flow of $7.65 billion and bought back shares worth $6.82 billion.

Adobe ended the period with $5.64 billion in cash and short-term investments. It fully used its previous $25 billion program, while $24.55 billion remained under a new $25 billion authorization approved in April 2026 and valid through April 2030.

The business also appears capable of supporting cash generation. Adobe's third-quarter revenues rose 12.9% year over year to $6.76 billion, while subscription revenues increased 13.7% to $6.56 billion. Annualized recurring revenues reached $27.5 billion, and remaining performance obligations totaled $22.16 billion, offering visibility into future revenues.

Record cash flow, recurring revenues and a sizable authorization give Adobe the flexibility to sustain meaningful repurchases. Buybacks can support earnings per share and offset stock-based compensation dilution.

How Do ADSK and CRM Compare With ADBE on Buybacks?

Autodesk, Inc. ADSK, a design-software peer, generated $518 million in operating cash flow and $505 million in free cash flow in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. During the first three quarters of fiscal 2027, the company generated operating cash flow of $1.99 billion and bought back shares worth $1.25 billion.

Autodesk's strong top-line growth is supporting product investment and shareholder returns. In the third quarter, Autodesk's revenues soared 12% year over year to $2.07 billion. The company expects to repurchase $1.5 billion worth of its common stock in full fiscal 2027, above its earlier expectations and higher than the share buybacks of $1.4 billion in fiscal 2026.

Salesforce, Inc. CRM competes with Adobe in the digital marketing and customer-experience software market. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Salesforce's operating cash flow jumped 71.5% year over year to $1.27 billion, while free cash flow increased 81.5% to $1.10 billion. In the first half of fiscal 2027, the company generated operating and free cash flows of $7.97 billion and $7.65 billion, respectively.

Salesforce Is 28% Off Its High: Why Guggenheim Still Sees 55% Upside Ahead of Earnings ©@ShutterOK from Getty Images Pro via Canva, @Blue Planet Studio from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Guggenheim reiterated its Buy rating and $300 target on Salesforce on Nov. 24, 55% above that day's close, after surveying 50 Salesforce partners.

Salesforce is 28% below its 52-week high, with organic revenue growth of 6% last quarter and Citi warning of slow demand for its core products.

Salesforce trades at about the same forward multiple as HubSpot, which is guiding to 12% growth, and well below ServiceNow, which grew subscriptions 21%.

The $300 target needs the multiple to climb about 35% as well as earnings to grow, so the Dec. 2 report matters more than usual.

Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) closed at $193.26 on Nov. 24, still 28% below its 52-week high. That same day, Guggenheim's John DiFucci reiterated his Buy rating and $300 target, 55% above the close, after surveying 50 Salesforce partners.

The stock is cheap for a reason. At 12.6x forward earnings on Nov. 23, Salesforce traded about level with HubSpot(HUBS:NYSE) at 12.3x, and HubSpot is guiding fourth-quarter revenue growth to just 12%. ServiceNow (NOW:NYSE), which grew subscription revenue 21% last quarter, gets 20.2x.

Salesforce's Organic Growth Hasn't Turned Yet

Second-quarter revenue rose 11% to $11.3 billion, but $456 million of that came from Informatica. Without it, revenue grew about 6%. CFO Robin Washington said in the Aug. 26 release that Salesforce is "on track for second-half organic revenue reacceleration."

The market isn't waiting. Salesforce fell 9% on Nov. 17 as software stocks slid ahead of Anthropic's IPO, and on Nov. 23 Citi cut its target to $198 from $263, keeping its Neutral rating after its checks pointed to slow demand for Salesforce's core products.

Guggenheim's Partners Sound Steadier

DiFucci has been here before. When he upgraded the stock in July, he argued that "the Armageddon scenario currently priced into the stock is misaligned with reality." His latest survey found a relatively stable environment, with modest improvement from the prior quarter. Not every bull has held on: BTIG cut its target to $250 from $300 on Nov. 18, though it kept its Buy rating.

Does $300 Add Up for Salesforce Stock?

The Street's average target has fallen to $284 from $330 a year ago, but it's still 47% above the price.
